stem: A design calls for application servers in a private subnet to download security patches from the internet on their own schedule, but nothing on the internet should ever be able to initiate a connection to those servers. Which component belongs in the design?

choices.text: A security group rule on the application servers allowing all outbound traffic
An internet gateway attached directly to the private subnet's route table
A NAT gateway placed in a public subnet, with the private subnet's route table pointing to it
A network ACL rule on the private subnet allowing outbound traffic on port 443

rationale: A NAT gateway sits in a public subnet with an Elastic IP, and a private subnet's route table can point its outbound default route at it, which lets the application servers start outbound connections such as patch downloads while remaining unreachable from any inbound connection initiated from the internet. Attaching an internet gateway directly to the private subnet's route table would give the subnet a two-way route to the internet, making it reachable from outside and directly contradicting the no-inbound requirement. A security group rule only controls what is allowed to and from the servers themselves; if the subnet's route table has no path to the internet at all, an outbound-allow security group rule still cannot get the traffic there. A network ACL rule on the subnet works the same way: it can permit outbound traffic on a port, but it does not create a route to the internet, so patches still could not be downloaded without a NAT gateway in place.
